newsitem.title: JAPAN: Forex markets should reflect fundamentals - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Forex markets should reflect fundamentals - MOF.

text.p: Currency markets should reflect economic fundamentals and radical fluctuations are troublesome, a senior official at Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) told Reuters on Thursday.
Asked whether MOF had changed its currency policy in the face of a recent dollar rise against the yen, the official said:
"There has been no change in stance due to any special factors."

But the official said the ministry is closely monitoring the currency market, in which, he said, sentiment is becoming nervous as a result of various events, such as the elections in Japan and the United States and the release of key economic data.

The dollar plunged in Tokyo on Thursday as comments by influential MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara led market participants to believe Japan had altered its policy of seeking a strong dollar, dealers said.
The dollar started Asian trade at 113.80 yen, but tumbled as low as 112.01 yen after the remarks.
The dollar's slide was first set off by reported comments by Sakakibara, the director-general of MOF's International Finance Bureau, dealers said.

Sakakibara was quoted in the Nikkei Financial Daily as saying the dollar's correction of its plunge against the yen last year was about to finish. He also said MOF was not trying to push the yen down further, the paper said.
Sakakibara later said the ministry was closely watching current developments in the foreign exchange market, but declined to comment either on specific currency levels or the newspaper article.
Dealers said they saw the absence of a denial as a sign that MOF was no longer willing to let the dollar head higher, and rushed to unload their accumulated dollars.
